body:
Independent publication review found a minor rerun-safety defect in three temporary round103 helpers. `push-pr.py` and `archive.py` reserved their final receipt only after remote or archive mutations. `create-issues.py` used a stale precreation issue snapshot and reserved its aggregate receipt only after creating issues, so replay could duplicate the already-created source follow-ups before refusing the occupied receipt.

These are temporary publication-tooling defects, not scientific record errors. The real source helper ran once and created #385–390; its successful receipt must remain unchanged. Neither real push-PR nor archive helper has run yet. Isolated stub tests reproduce the original post-effect failure without touching GitHub or the real archive.

Acceptance:

- Reserve each final receipt exclusively before any side effect; refuse existing ordinary files, valid symlinks and dangling symlinks without mutation.
- Retain the owned receipt handle and write a terminal success or failure outcome, including partial execution evidence.
- Verify with isolated subprocess stubs that replay causes no remote/archive effects and preserves existing bytes and link identity. Exercise successful empty-path execution and failure after reservation separately.
- Save exact original/corrected hashes, regression evidence and independent disposition under `reviews/publication/20261015-round103/`; do not rerun the real issue creator.

Initial finding: `/private/tmp/cmm-round103-helper-audit/20261015T212520Z-template-guard-assessment.json`, key `receipt-reservation-before-mutations`; the package review independently identified the analogous issue-creator path. This issue tracks those concrete corrections; broader transaction rollback is outside its scope.
title: Reserve publication receipts before remote or archive mutations
